Religion by the Doctors of Schoole-Divinity, might be
produced ; but other men may if they please observe
them of themselves. I shall onely adde this, that the

(as I have said once before) see whether he can translate
any Schoole-Divine into any of the Modern tongues, as
French, English, or any other copious language: for
that which cannot in most of these be made Intelligible,
is not Intelligible in the Latine. Which Insignificancy of
language, though I cannot note it for false Philosophy ;
yet it hath a quality, not onely to hide the Truth, but
also to make men think they have it, and desist from
further search.
